## About

I'm a frontend-focused software engineer with 10 years of experience building and maintaining complex web applications. Beyond shipping features, I've helped make architecture decisions, co-led framework migrations, and written the guidelines that help teams deliver consistently.

Most of my recent work is in React, Next.js and Material UI. At J.D. Power I improved the Core Web Vitals of jdpower.com over several months, and tracked down a Google Ads issue that had been affecting the site for months.

I have also worked across the stack: Node.js backends, a horizontally scalable server provisioning system and a two-tier cache that halved S3 costs at modd.io, plus mobile apps in React Native and Flutter.

I started at JumpByte (now AppGambit) shortly after graduating from Uka Tarsadia University, working on a wide variety of projects.

## Case studies

### Leading a multi-framework frontend migration (J.D. Power)

What started as a Next.js upgrade on jdpower.com turned into a coordinated migration across Next.js, React and Material UI. I co-led the effort with the team.

- Problem: The jdpower.com frontend needed a Next.js upgrade to keep the stack current.
- Discovery: Upgrading Next.js meant upgrading React, and that in turn required moving Material UI from v4 to v5. The Material UI migration proved to be a much larger undertaking than the original upgrade.
- Decision: As a team, we decided to tackle the Material UI migration first. I took part in that architectural decision and helped set the implementation approach and timeline.
- My contribution: I documented the easiest migration paths and the technical issues developers were likely to hit, wrote guidelines for current and future development, and guided other developers through the migration.
- Outcome: Material UI and Next.js were upgraded, and the guidelines remained in place for later frontend work.

## Core Web Vitals results at J.D. Power

- Mobile: "Good" URLs +197%, "Poor" URLs -96%
- Desktop: "Good" URLs +168%, "Poor" URLs -21%

## Experience

### Senior Frontend Developer — J.D. Power (November 2022 - Present)

Company: https://jdpower.com

- Maintained jdpower.com, a Next.js web application that connects users with car dealers or with other users who want to sell their cars.
- Co-led the Material UI v4 → v5 and Next.js upgrades: helped decide to tackle the larger Material UI migration first, set the approach and timeline, documented migration paths and likely issues, and guided other developers through the work.
- Wrote frontend guidelines for future development as part of the migration.
- Helped migrate from the Pages Router to the App Router in Next.js.
- Debugged a Google Ads issue that had affected the site for months, and streamlined the implementation so Google no longer served empty ads.
- Helped choose and integrate the analytics tools used in production.
- Improved the overall performance and Core Web Vitals of the application by carefully optimizing the codebase over several months.
  - Mobile: increased "Good" URLs by 197% and reduced "Poor" URLs by 96%.
  - Desktop: increased "Good" URLs by 168% and reduced "Poor" URLs by 21%.

## Projects

### Smart Copy

Smart Copy explores one problem across native and cross-platform apps: keeping copied text and notes accessible wherever you work. I built Android, Angular, React, and React Native implementations, including a Node.js backend and a Firebase-backed PWA.

Stack: Android, Angular, React, React Native, Firebase
- Demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BB-6VMgOwFc
- Code: https://github.com/NishantDesai1306/react-native-smart-copy
- Android (Native): Smart Copy started from this project. On native Android I used the platform's floating window, so whenever a user double-clicks any input field in any app, a dismissible floating bubble pops up showing all copied items in a floating list.
- Angular App: A mobile-responsive web companion to the mobile app, built with Angular v6. It connects to the same database, so everything you copy in the Android app is also accessible on the web. I also wrote the NodeJS backend server that serves the data to the app.
- React App: Another mobile-responsive web companion to the original Smart Copy app, built with React. It is also a PWA, so you can install it on other smartphones or as a desktop app. It uses Firebase for file storage (profile pictures) and Firestore as the backend to store and retrieve items.
- React Native: A simple React Native mobile app that supports user accounts and shows a list of items you can edit or delete. I started this project to learn more about hybrid mobile frameworks that let me build the same app for Android and iOS.

### Chess

A chess application built with React and Node.js. I integrated Stockfish 15 to show a position evaluation bar alongside the board, combining a focused interface with chess-engine feedback.

Stack: React, NodeJS, Bootstrap, Stockfish 15
- Code: https://github.com/NishantDesai1306/chess

### Chatzz

Chatzz is a Socket.io-based chat framework: a reusable Node.js foundation for adding real-time messaging to a chat application.

Stack: Socket.io, NodeJS
- Code: https://github.com/NishantDesai1306/chatzz

### YouTube Subscriber Counter

A cross-platform Flutter app for comparing the subscriber counts of two YouTube channels, exploring a shared mobile UI framework.

Stack: Flutter
- Demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RwFfTf3dJww
- Code: https://github.com/NishantDesai1306/youtube_channel_sub_counter/tree/master
